title: Udbud af rammeaftale vedrørende levering af pædagogiske vikarer til Hillerød Kommune
description: Udbuddet omfatter levering af pædagogiske vikarer til daginstitutioner i Hillerød Kommune. Ydelserne omfatter alene vikartimer afholdt i dagtimer på hverdage inden for følgende kategorier af vikarer:PædagogerPædagogmedhjælperePædagogiske assistenterAftalen er rettet mod Ordregivers daginstitutioner, der har et behov for vikarer. Ordregiver kan og vil indgå aftaler om levering af pædagogiske vikarer rettet mod andre typer af behov og afdelinger, som fx vikarer til botilbud og andre særtilbud.Aftalen omfatter er rettet mod levering af vikarer, når Ordregivers eget vikarkorps samt Ordregivers faste pædagoger, pædagogmedhjælpere mv. ikke kan dække behovet. Krav til vikarerne samt vilkår for bestilling og levering fremgår af Aftalen med tilhørende bilag - herunder særligt Bilag 1 – Kravspecifikation.Der arbejdes med to overordnede typer af vikarbestillinger: Akutvikarer og Planlagte Vikarer.Aftalen giver ikke vindende tilbudsgiver krav på eller garanti for et bestemt antal timer/vagter. Leverancernes omfang bestemmes alene af de bestillinger, som de enkelte Bestillere hos Ordregiver løbende afgiver. Forbruget er således bestemt af det faktiske behov for i Ordregivers afdelinger og institutioner, og Ordregiver er ikke forpligtet til at aftage et vist minimum.Der er i Aftalen krav om en minimumsleveringsgrad, hvorved menes, hvor stor en procentdel af alle bestillinger som den vindende tilbudsgiver skal dække.Kravene er en leveringsgrad på 92 % for Akutvikarer og 95 % for Planlagte vikarer. Såfremt de fastsatte leveringsgrader ikke overholdes, vil der være tale om mislighold der blandt andet vil kunne medføre et krav om betaling af en bod.

description: Am Bildungsstandort Eslohe befindet sich das zentrale Kompetenzzentrum des Dachdeckerhandwerks in Westfalen. Die bestehende Gebäudeinfrastruktur stammt überwiegend aus den Jahren 1968 und 1985. Im Rahmen einer Machbarkeitsstudie wurden verschiedene Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten für den Standort untersucht. Auf Grundlage der Ergebnisse hat sich der Auftraggeber für die Realisierung eines Ersatzneubaukonzeptes entschieden. Damit sollen die funktionalen, organisatorischen, pädagogischen und energetischen Anforderungen langfristig erfüllt und gleichzeitig der laufende Schul- und Wohnheimbetrieb während der Realisierung sichergestellt werden.

title: Rocket Systems Launch Program (RSLP) Innovative Delivery of Effects (RIDE) Supplemental Request for Information (RFI) � Industry Statements of Capability (SOCs)
description: Rocket Systems Launch Program (RSLP) Innovative Delivery of Effects (RIDE) Supplemental Request for Information (RFI) � Industry Statements of Capability (SOCs): 1. RIDE Overview (Updated): The Space Systems Command (SSC), System Delta 80 (SYD 80), Small Launch and Targets Division (AMX) manages the Rocket Systems Launch Program (RSLP). Supplemental to the previous RFI posted on 25 April 2025 (https://sam.gov/opp/19f4b8b3647940b48fa14134d23249a9/view#contact), RSLP still plans to execute its suborbital and orbital launch services by employing its new RSLP Innovative Delivery of Effects (RIDE) acquisition strategy. RIDE acquisitions will serve as the next generation of RSLP launch service contracts, succeeding the Orbital Services Program-4 (OSP-4), Small Rocket Program-Orbital (SRP-O), and Sounding Rocket Program-4 (SRP-4) programs. RSLP will continue to provide responsive space, experimental, Research, Development, Test and Evaluation (RDT&E), and small operational launch vehicles and targets support to the Department of War (DoW) and other Government agencies using commercial services and excess ballistic missile assets. RIDE acquisitions are intended to support a wide variety of customer-driven requirements that may not traditionally fall within the scope of NSSL requirements, from integration and launch of payloads intended for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and beyond, to suborbital vehicle development, and more. Given the variety of launch missions with varying degrees of complexity that RSLP anticipates supporting, the RIDE acquisition strategy may result in one (1) or more contract vehicles [such as an indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract, which is currently being considered]. In response to industry feedback captured by RSLP�s first RFI solicitation, Attachment 1 of this RFI contains updated high-level requirements of the RIDE acquisition strategy. These requirements are still subject to change. 2. Background (Unchanged): RSLP has historically launched one-off launch systems for RDT&E type payloads, from unguided lofted trajectories to cis-lunar orbit. In the past, industry offered limited launch service options capable of meeting the wide range of mission performance required. This led to RSLP managing many first-flight vehicles, or vehicles with first-flight items, to meet our customers� needs. The management of those first-flight vehicles and items shaped the mission assurance practices that RSLP implemented and continues to use today. Our customers, mainly from the RDT&E community with limited budgets, drive mission assurance requirements based on their risk tolerance. A higher level of risk is more often deemed acceptable for the payloads than for the launch vehicles. RSLP recognizes that industry�s capability and capacity have changed greatly over the last 10 years. RSLP is therefore assessing those changes and determining how to best meet the launch service needs of our U.S. Government customers. There is a wide variance in the experience, vehicle heritage, and production and manufacturing processes observed across the commercial launch industry today. This variance offers opportunities to ensure fair competition while providing varying levels of mission assurance across different customer requirement driven missions. 3. RIDE Acquisition Background (Added): RIDE is intended to enable RSLP to provide an encompassing launch service acquisition solution in support of the United States Space Force (USSF), DoW, and other Government customers. In doing so, it is anticipated that RIDE will provide a means to support both Space Transportation Services [as defined in 51 U.S. Code � 50101(4); which are considered inherently commercial in accordance with 51 U.S. Code � 50132] and Space-Related Activity launch services [as defined in 51 U.S. Code � 50101(3); which are�for the purposes of this contemplated acquisition strategy�not assumed to be inherently commercial] required by various programs with various payloads. Space Transportation Services involve the preparation as well as transportation of a launch vehicle and its payloads to, from, or within outer space, or in suborbital trajectory. Space-Related Activity launch services include research and development (R&D), which is more in-depth or complex than a traditional Space Transportation Service. Additionally, Space-Related Activity launch services may require new design, significant modifications, extensive supplemental qualification testing, and/or developmental concept of operations (CONOPs). To support both Space Transportation and Space-Related Activity launches, the Government is contemplating the use of two (2) multiple-award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract vehicles; one (1) for Space Transportation Services and [commercial] Space-Related Activity launch services and one (1) for [non-commercial] Space-Related Activity launch services: Space Transportation Services will be procured as a commercial service, leveraging commercial practices on a fixed-price [e.g., Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), fixed-price incentive, fixed-price with award fee, etc.] basis. Additionally, certain Space-Related Activity services which are determined to be commercial by the cognizant Procurement Contracting Officer (PCO) at the time of the contemplated effort shall also be acquired under the commercial IDIQ and will also utilize a fixed-price structure. Due to the developmental/non-commercial nature of many of the anticipated Space-Related Activity services, the Government anticipates issuing hybrid cost-reimbursement [e.g., Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Cost-Plus-Incentive-Fee (CPIF), cost-reimbursement incentive, cost-plus award fee, etc.] and FFP task orders under the non-commercial IDIQ, as appropriate for the specific requirement (again, to be decided by the cognizant PCO at the time of the contemplated effort). Companies should consider whether they possess, or can obtain, the systems and capabilities necessary to perform cost-reimbursement contracts, including an improved accounting system IAW R-DFARS 242.7502 (implemented by 48 CFR 242.7502) and comply with the system criteria prescribed in R-DFARS 252.242-7998 (if applicable) and DFARS 252.242.7999 (Deviation 2026-O0050) (March 2026). A company may compete for entry into the vendor pool of one (1) or both IDIQs, but must follow and satisfy the proposal requirements for each IDIQ if they wish to compete for both. 4. title: Modernization and Engineering Support - III (MES III)
description: The Air National Guard (ANG) Air Force Reserve Command Test Center (AATC) is a unit of the ANG stationed at Tucson Air National Guard Base (ANGB), AZ with operating locations at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base (AFB), AZ; Eglin AFB, FL; Little Rock AFB, AR; Roland R. Wright ANGB, UT; and Hancock Field ANGB, NY. AATC conducts operational test and evaluation (OT&E) for the Air Reserve Component (ARC) and other Major Commands (MAJCOMs) exercising lead command authority over a variety of ARC possessed Mission Design Series (MDS) systems and associated weapons, sensors, and support equipment. These ARC aircraft and systems are older and require low cost, off-the-shelf modernization updates to maintain combat capabilities. AATC has engineering and test responsibility for the National Guard Bureau (NGB) and Air Force Reserve Command (AFRC). In this role, AATC is responsible for working with Air Force Material Command (AFMC), system program offices (SPOs), and other related engineering offices to conduct research, development, test, and evaluation to determine the operational suitability and effectiveness of candidate developmental sensors and systems that address the modernization requirements identified in the annual Air National Guard Weapons System Modernization Priorities Book, and Air Force Reserve Modernization Book as well as requirements provided to AATC by the MAJCOMs. There are currently over 100 active projects at AATC supporting A-10, C-130, F-15, F-35, F-16, C-17, KC-135, KC-46, HH-60, HC/MC-130, MQ-9, Special Warfare (SW), Cyber, and multiple cross-platform logistics and electronic warfare (EW) capabilities. The average lifetime of most projects is six months to three years from concept approval to final report and initial fielding, but complexity may shorten or extend the amount of time required to complete the project. Expertise for each of these platforms and capability areas is required to ensure successful testing of modernization capabilities. Skill set requirements may be transferable or adjusted as projects are completed and new projects are started. Required technical expertise includes but is not limited to: operational and maintenance experience on specific platforms, expertise or familiarization with platform systems, integration and modification experience, developmental and operational test experience, airworthiness and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approvals, assisting the Government with technical requirements definition, cost assessment and control, executing aircraft avionics integration, systems engineering, design engineering, creating integrated logistics support such as technical orders, flight manuals, job guides, and software manuals, and program engineering coordination necessary to support ANG and AFRC modification programs. New projects may need additional expertise as they are approved in the annual United States Air Force Reserve Modernization Book and ANG Weapons Systems Modernization Priorities Book. These books are available online and identify modernization priorities and projects this PWS will support. As modernization priorities and projects are approved and funded, AATC will conduct OT&E activities to determine the validity of solutions and make fielding recommendations, as required. The contractor will support this process through all phases from concept development, test planning, test execution, and final report delivery. The ability to develop briefings, write test plans, conduct tests, and deliver comprehensive final reports is required. The contractor shall perform test planning, test execution, data analysis, test reporting, test logistics and studies/analysis for modernization installations and integration on ARC platforms which are composed of the ANG and AFRC weapons systems. In addition, the contractor shall perform specialized System Under Test (SUT) acquisition, program management, integration engineering, engineering liaison, and technology insertion to assist AATC and NGB/A5 with modernization of ARC weapons systems to include but not limited to aircraft, Joint Terminal Area Controller (JTAC) and Special Warfare, Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C4ISR), domestic operations, cyber security, logistics programs software support, and test process training support. ARC modernization efforts require avionics, mechanical, and structural modifications to include but not limited to technical requirements definition, avionics integration, systems engineering, design engineering, test support, integrated logistics engineering, studies and analyses, cybersecurity approval, prototype installations, program engineering coordination, test equipment, and technical documentation. Participation in integrated product teams (IPTs) within the Department of Defense (DoD) communities will be required to accomplish the assigned tasks. The products and support will be provided to several customers including AATC, MAJCOMs, Air Force and other DoD stakeholders to include the Aeronautical Systems Center (ASC) and Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) supported programs, Air Force Life Cycle Management Centers (AFLCM) program offices, and Joint Program Offices (JPO).

description: East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust (ESNEFT) is inviting qualified Suppliers to express an interest to participate in a tender exercise for; Charitable Funds Investment under the Procurement Act 2023. This expression of interest will require interested parties to: - Confirm interest - Complete and submit capability assessment attachment The Capability Assessment submitted by interested parties will be reviewed to identify appropriate Suppliers to invite to tender. Invitation to Tender (ITT) with project timelines to be issued upon successful pass of this Capability Assessment stage. The Trust will aim to issue the ITT in October 2026. The top four suppliers, based on the evaluation of their ITT submissions, will be invited to interview with the Trust. Accordingly, all suppliers should be advised that interviews are provisionally scheduled for the afternoon of 16 November 2026. As this date has been agreed with key stakeholders, it is not expected to change. East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust (ESNEFT) is the largest NHS organisation in its region, formed on July 1, 2018, through the merger of Colchester Hospital University NHS Foundation Trust and The Ipswich Hospital NHS Trust. ESNEFT provides comprehensive hospital and community healthcare services across multiple locations, including Colchester, Ipswich, Clacton, Halstead, Harwich, Felixstowe, and Aldeburgh. The trust offers a wide range of medical services such as acute medicine, cardiology, dermatology, emergency assessment, gastroenterology, neurology, and many more. ESNEFT is committed to delivering high-quality care and continuously improving its facilities and services to meet the needs of the local communities. Every year hundreds of individuals, community groups and businesses generously donate money to help us achieve our aims. It is our job to make sure that the money is spent carefully and for the purposes for which it was given. The ESNEFT Charity holds designated charitable funds for many of the services in the hospital as well as appeal funds. They have a duty to maximise the value it gets from public donation, but without exposure to undue levels of risk. We do not have the skills in house therefore appoint advisors to assist us with this. The Charity's existing portfolio is invested in Ethical investment funds, property funds and a common deposit fund. ESNEFT is looking to re-procure the management and advice of The Trusts Charitable Funds Investment. title: Hydraulic Press Small Arms Demilitarization System �Commodore Crunch� Maintenance and Repair Services in Anniston, Alabama
description: DLA Disposition Services intends to award a sole source contract according to FAR Part 6 and FAR Part 12 to CNC Solutions LLC (CAGE: JTR6). The acquisition is pursued according to procedures in FAR 6.103-1(b), 12.102(b) and 12.201-1. The services for this contract will provide critical preventative maintenance and correct maintenance to the Commodore Crunch system to demilitarize Department of War excess property. Due to the high customization, expertise, and experience of maintaining this equipment, DLA Disposition Services is conducting a sole source action to award this contract to CNC Solutions to perform the maintenance services. Maintenance services are required for the Hydraulic Press Small Arms Demilitarization System, informally known as �Commodore Crunch.� The Hydraulic Press is necessary for demilitarization functions at DLA DS Anniston site. Hydraulic Press operability is imperative to the site�s mission to prevent backlog of material requiring demilitarization. The Contractor shall troubleshoot, diagnose, provide scheduled maintenance, obtain parts, and repair the hydraulic press. The maintenance / repair of this highly specialized equipment is deemed to be available only from the original source, CNC Solutions. Acquisition planning supports this is a sole source requirement. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR [RFO] 12.102(b). This proposed contract will be a Sole Source acquisition under NAICS code 811310 with a size standard of $12.5M. The Justification and Approval (J&A) is attached to this posting [Attachment 1]. The J&A was prepared according to FAR 6.104. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. A solicitation document will not be issued, and quotes will not be requested. All Federal Acquisition Regulation references in this notice are according to the FAR Overhaul [RFO].

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Grundhafte Erneuerung von drei innerörtlichen Straßen (Liederbach)
description: Zur Verbesserung der örtlichen Verkehrsinfrastruktur plant die Stadt Alsfeld die grundhafte Erneuerung der Merschroder Straße sowie die Sanierung bzw. Erneuerung des Brückenbauwerks über den Liederbach. Für die gemeindeeigene Straße In der Hohl sind je nach Ausbauabschnitt entweder eine grundhafte Erneuerung oder ein erstmaliger Ausbau vorgesehen. Auf Grundlage des vorhandenen baulichen Zustands besteht in allen zwei Straßenbereichen ein erheblicher Erneuerungsbedarf. Darüber hinaus ist der Straßenendausbau der Straße Hainberg geplant. Die Merschroder Straße weist deutliche Schäden an der Fahrbahnoberfläche in Form von Rissen, Setzungen und Unebenheiten auf. Auch die Gehwege, Nebenanlagen sowie die vorhandenen Entwässerungseinrichtungen entsprechen nicht mehr den aktuellen funktionalen und barrierefreien Anforderungen. Die Straße In der Hohl befindet sich ebenfalls in einem stark sanierungsbedürftigen Zustand und zudem noch nicht vollständig ausgebaut. Da die Straße Hainberg derzeit noch keinen endgültigen Ausbauzustand aufweist, soll sie im Zuge der Maßnahme vollständig ausgebaut werden. Ein weiterer Bestandteil der Maßnahme ist die Erneuerung des Plattenbrückenbauwerks, die sich im südlichen Abschnitt der Merschroder Straße befindet und die über den Liederbach führt. Das Ingenieurbauwerk weist alters- und nutzungsbedingte Defizite im Über- sowie Unterbau auf und soll im Zuge der Gesamtmaßnahme planerisch berücksichtigt sowie je nach Untersuchungsergebnis erneuert oder ertüchtigt werden.

title: Netherlands – Advertising and marketing services – Arbeidsmarktcommunicatie en Mediadiensten

Opdrachtnemer voert deze werkzaamheden uit voor (arbeidsmarkt)campagnes en losse plaatsingen van de Politie. De mediaplaatsingen vinden hoofdzakelijk plaats in Nederlandse media, maar de Politie heeft met betrekking tot opsporingscommunicatie ook behoefte aan plaatsingen in buitenlandse media (voornamelijk binnen Europa). Arbeidsmarktcommunicatie heeft als doel het positioneren van de Politie als aantrekkelijke werkgever en opleider ten behoeve van de werving van voldoende agenten, bedrijfsvoeringsfuncties en diverse andere (specialistische) politiefuncties. Om dat te bereiken ontwikkelt de Politie samen met de Opdrachtnemer voor arbeidsmarktcommunicatie onder andere wervingscampagnes. Om deze campagnes op het juiste moment bij de juiste doelgroepen te laten landen werkt de Opdrachtnemer voor arbeidsmarkt-communicatie intensief samen met de Opdrachtnemer voor mediadiensten. Het mediabureau adviseert over de in te zetten media, heeft kennis van mediagedrag van uiteenlopende doelgroepen, monitort de prestaties van de ingezette campagne-uitingen en stemt dit weer af met de Politie of met het arbeidsmarktcommunicatiebureau om daarmee de campagnes te optimaliseren.

title: Netherlands – Blood-testing reagents – Levering en implementatie van en onderhoud aan een gevalideerde Totaaloplossing voor de SCID- en SMA-screening ten behoeve van meerdere laboratoria
description: De neonatale hielprikscreening (NHS) is een landelijk screeningsprogramma dat wordt uitgevoerd bij pasgeborenen in de eerste week na de geboorte. In Nederland (Europees en Caribisch Nederland) krijgen jaarlijks ca. 170.000 pasgeborenen de hielprik. De hielprikscreening is het langstlopende landelijke screeningsprogramma in de publieke gezondheidszorg. De analyse van het hielprikbloed levert op dit moment belangrijke informatie op over zevenentwintig zeldzame, vaak erfelijke, ernstige aandoeningen. Het bloedonderzoek wordt vanaf 2026 verricht door drie screeningslaboratoria, waarvan het screeningslaboratorium van RIVM-GZB fungeert als referentielaboratorium. De screeningslaboratoria zijn verantwoordelijk voor de analyse van het hielprikbloedmonster en een tijdige rapportage van de uitslag. In alle screeningslaboratoria wordt vanaf januari 2021 onder meer gebruik gemaakt van een Totaaloplossing voor de screening op SCID. Vanaf 1 juni 2022 is ook SMA toegevoegd aan het programma en screenen de laboratoria met een multiplex Totaaloplossing waarmee zowel op SCID als SMA gescreend kan worden. Daarnaast bestaat de mogelijkheid dat in de komende jaren besloten wordt dat op X-gebonden Agammaglobulinemie (XLA) gescreend moet gaan worden. Om de uniformiteit te borgen heeft het RIVM besloten om de apparaten (hardware), software, reagentia en bijbehorend onderhoud (preventief, correctief, adaptief), ook wel Totaaloplossing genoemd, in te kopen en ter beschikking te stellen aan de screeningslaboratoria. Deze Aanbestedingsprocedure betreft een opdracht voor de levering, implementatie en onderhoud van een gevalideerde Totaaloplossing voor de SCID- en SMA-screening voor de screeningslaboratoria. Het doel van deze Europese aanbesteding is het sluiten van een Overeenkomst met één Opdrachtnemer, volgens het principe van reagent rental waarbij de leverancier eigenaar blijft van de apparatuur. De Opdrachtnemer wordt volledig verantwoordelijk voor het leveren, implementeren en doorlopend ter beschikking stellen van de Totaaloplossing en het verrichten van daaraan verwante diensten overeenkomstig de specificaties die zijn neergelegd in de Aanbestedingsstukken.

title: Netherlands – Environmental engineering consultancy services – Ondersteuning stikstofadvies, -modellering en -informatiesystemen 2027
description: Algemene informatie Aanbestedende dienst Het Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu (RIVM) is een agentschap van het Ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport (VWS). Het RIVM bevordert door onderzoek, uitvoering en ondersteuning de publieke gezondheid en een schoon en veilig leefmilieu. Tot de kerntaken van dit instituut behoort beleidsondersteuning voor de overheid. Deze diensten worden in zowel nationale als internationale context uitgevoerd. Het RIVM bestaat uit een dertigtal onderdelen, meestal laboratoria, teams of centra met een specifieke onderzoekstaak. Het domein Milieu & Veiligheid (M&V) ontwikkelt kennis en kunde en adviseert overheden over een veilige en gezonde leefomgeving. Dit domein controleert bijvoorbeeld de kwaliteit van lucht, water en bodem. En doet metingen na een ongeluk of ramp, waarbij mogelijk gevaarlijke stoffen vrijkomen. Het onderzoekt verschillende vormen van straling, zoals radioactieve stoffen, lichtbronnen, hoogspanningslijnen en mobiele telefoons. En het onderzoekt de effecten van omgevingsfactoren op de gezondheid, zoals luchtverontreiniging of geluidhinder. M&V doet ook onderzoek naar perceptie en gedrag. Als onderdeel van het domein M&V brengt Centrum Milieukwaliteit (MIL) de kwaliteit van het fysieke milieu in beeld. Het gaat dan vooral over de kwaliteit van bodem, grondwater en lucht, en van omgevingsfactoren zoals geluid en licht. Dit doet MIL door meting (monitoring) en door berekening (modellering). MIL signaleert trends en brengt de effecten van beleidsmaatregelen op de milieukwaliteit in kaart. De kwaliteit van het milieu in Nederland staat in nauwe relatie met internationale ontwikkelingen. Daarom is MIL betrokken bij de internationale milieumonitoring voor het European Environmental Agency en klimaatonderzoek. Hieronder zijn een aantal voorbeeldteksten vermeld, aanpassen aan domein / centrum / afdeling waarvoor de aanbesteding wordt uitgevoerd. Indien het een aanbesteding voor de categorie laboratorium betreft: RIVM teksten verwijderen. Indien RIVM de aanbesteding uitvoert ten behoeve van de categorie laboratorium onderstaande alinea opnemen en de namen en korte beschrijving van de opdrachtgevers vermelden (zie voor teksten het document ‘Algemene informatie deelnemers categore Lab v2’). Indien geen categorie aanbesteding, onderstaande alinea verwijderen. title: Norway – Hotel services – Framework agreement for course- and conference services.
description: The contracting authority is the Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority (henceforth also referred to as the Contracting Authority or the Customer). The Norwegian Labour Inspection Authority is a government agency under the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs.
